chains.summary: The joy one grows into by practice, like poison first and nectar in the end, is born of a clear understanding of the self. Pleasure from the senses is nectar first and poison after. The pleasure of sleep, laziness and heedlessness deludes from start to finish.
chains.title: Poison first, nectar after

verses.m: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
verses.sa: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥

verses.m: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
verses.sa: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥

verses.m: The happiness that comes from contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called rajasic.
verses.sa: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥

chains.summary: A person moves among things with senses controlled, free of attraction and aversion, and reaches clarity. In clarity sorrows end and understanding steadies. Without that steadiness there is no peace, and without peace there is no happiness.
chains.title: The ladder of ascent

verses.m: But a disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, attains clarity and calm.
In that clarity all sorrows come to an end; for one whose mind is clear, understanding soon becomes steady.
verses.sa: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥

verses.m: For the undisciplined there is no understanding and no steady contemplation. Without contemplation there is no peace, and for the one without peace, where is happiness?
verses.sa: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥

chains.summary: A person lets go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, without the sense of mine and at peace, and becomes fit for Brahman. In that state one neither grieves nor craves, is the same to all beings, and gains the highest devotion.
chains.title: Serene, neither grieving nor craving

verses.m: Become one with Brahman, serene in self, one neither grieves nor craves. The same to all beings, one gains supreme devotion to me.
verses.sa: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥

chains.summary: By regret one is freed from the wrong done. By resolving I will not do it again one is freed from repeating it. Turning to good after a wrong, one comes out like the moon from behind a cloud.
chains.title: Regret, then resolve

verses.m: One who feels remorse for a wrong deed is freed from that wrong; by resolving 'I will not do it again', he is freed from the second.
verses.sa: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते

verses.m: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
verses.sa: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः

gloss: The clear, settled mind in which sorrows end and understanding steadies (2.64-65). This state is prasāda.

hero.m: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling: this is called austerity of the mind.

loci.m: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling: this is called austerity of the mind.
That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
loci.sa: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥

loci.m: But a disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, attains clarity and calm.

practices.m: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
practices.sa: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥
practices.why: Shows a light, friendly tone toward one's own mind.

practices.m: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, measured in effort at work, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
practices.sa: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
practices.why: A measured day makes the mind light enough for practice.

practices.m: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
practices.sa: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥

practices.m: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
practices.sa: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥

practices.m: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
practices.sa: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उर:स्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
practices.why: Gives a concrete picture of clear, unhurried speech.

practices.m: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling: this is called austerity of the mind.
practices.why: Shows serenity of mind named first.

practices.m: One who holds back the blazing anger stirred by an insult or a wounding slight, who stays clean-hearted, cheerful and free of envy, takes the merit of others.
practices.r: Hamsa Gita 11 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.11 in our data)
practices.sa: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥

practices.m: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are flavourful, soothing, nourishing and agreeable, are dear to the sattvic.
practices.sa: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
practices.why: Shows food chosen for clarity and cheer.

stories.l: Clarity, once found, turns into action.
stories.s: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.

stories.l: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.
stories.s: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.

stories.l: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.
stories.s: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

stories.l: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.
stories.s: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
